chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: The Billy Pierce Studio and its famous students
summary: Green lists the film and stage figures who studied or taught at the studio, and why Bradley took a rest in England.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Okay, why don't you explain to me a bit about the Buddy Bradley-Billy Pierce Studio, what it was like.
Well, it was the most famous dance studio in New York City at that time. This was in 1931, the

first of 1931, in February. See, because people like George M. Cohen -- by the way, James Cagney was teaching on the third floor also. He was a dance teacher in the Billy Pierce Studio, and he had students like Dan Dailey, Van Johnson, even James Stewart, he used to come there, see. And they -- they became very famous in moving pictures, you see, these people, which also happened to Eleanor Powell and Arlene Judge, Rita Hayworth, Lucille Ball, Joan Blondell -- she used to come there -- and Nancy Carroll, she was famous in the movies, Warner Brothers movie star.

And I think a friend of mine, Mr. Buddy Bradley's wife, you know, widow, Lady B. Bradley, she explained to me about Clifton Webb, you see. He was also a student of Buddy Bradley, and he was very popular. You know, George M. Cohen, he was a very popular man, famous for composing songs, putting on Broadway shows and all this, and that's really what Mr. Buddy Bradley was involved in at the time he left for England, because he was doing the choreographies for these great shows, these Broadway shows, and they weren't giving him the credits, you know, like someone -- I think they called him Busby Berkeley, and he was not a dancer, but he had Mr. Buddy Bradley doing the choreographies for those dance numbers in the movies, and he didn't give him credits, you know.
And so I think that's why Mr. Billy Pierce allowed Buddy Bradley to take this vacation like trip, you know. He
called it a rest, said he needed a rest because he was kind of overworked.
